review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

1:1.sourceText: Ἀρχὴ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ (Υἱοῦ Θεοῦ).
1:1.targetText: This is the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a presentational frame; the Greek title has no verb.

1:2.sourceText: Καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν τῷ Ἡσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου·
1:2.targetText: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet:  “Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.”

groups.note: The present ἀποστέλλω ("I send") is rendered as a future.
πρὸ προσώπου ("before the face of") is rendered ahead of.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:3.sourceText: φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν Κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ,
1:3.targetText: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:4.sourceText: ἐγένετο Ἰωάνης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν.
1:4.targetText: John the Baptist appeared in the wilderness, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.

groups.note: The article with the participle βαπτίζων ("the one baptizing") is rendered the Baptist.

1:5.sourceText: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία χώρα καὶ οἱ Ἱεροσολυμεῖται πάντες, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.
1:5.targetText: People went out to him from all of Jerusalem and the countryside of Judea. Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.

groups.note: BSB's one all stands for both πᾶσα (with the Judean countryside) and πάντες (with the Jerusalemites).
Ἱεροσολυμεῖται ("the people of Jerusalem") is rendered by the city name.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence with Confessing instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a general subject; in Greek the Judean countryside and the Jerusalemites are the subject.
English turns the Greek subjects into the place the people came from.

1:6.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ὁ Ἰωάνης ἐνδεδυμένος τρίχας καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσθων ἀκρίδας καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.
1:6.targetText: John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.

groups.note: The καί that adds the belt is rendered with.
The participle ἔσθων ("eating"), still governed by ἦν, is rendered His food was.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

1:7.sourceText: καὶ ἐκήρυσσεν λέγων Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς κύψας λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ.
1:7.targetText: And he began to proclaim: “After me will come One more powerful than I, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.

groups.note: The imperfect ἐκήρυσσεν is rendered began to proclaim.
The resumptive αὐτοῦ ("his") repeats the relative οὗ; English expresses both with whose.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων (saying) is represented only by the colon before the quotation.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle κύψας is rendered as a second infinitive, stoop down.

1:8.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ.
1:8.targetText: I baptize you with water, but He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”

groups.note: The aorist ἐβάπτισα is rendered with the English present.
N1904's plain dative gives with, as ὕδατι does; the publisher's Greek adds ἐν here.

1:9.sourceText: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάνου.
1:9.targetText: In those days Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the narrative formula καὶ ἐγένετο ("and it came about") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:10.sourceText: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος εἶδεν σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα ὡς περιστερὰν καταβαῖνον εἰς αὐτόν·
1:10.targetText: As soon as Jesus came up out of the water, He saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove.

groups.note: εὐθύς ("immediately") with the temporal participle ἀναβαίνων is rendered As soon as.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle ἀναβαίνων.

1:11.sourceText: καὶ φωνὴ ἐγένετο ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν Σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα.
1:11.targetText: And a voice came from heaven: “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:12.sourceText: Καὶ εὐθὺς τὸ Πνεῦμα αὐτὸν ἐκβάλλει εἰς τὴν ἔρημον.
1:12.targetText: At once the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness,

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

1:13.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τεσσεράκοντα ἡμέρας πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ, καὶ ἦν μετὰ τῶν θηρίων, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι διηκόνουν αὐτῷ.
1:13.targetText: and He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals, and the angels ministered to Him.

groups.note: BSB renders ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ ("in the wilderness"), just named in 1:12, as there.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

1:14.sourceText: Καὶ μετὰ τὸ παραδοθῆναι τὸν Ἰωάνην ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Θεοῦ
1:14.targetText: After the arrest of John, Jesus went into Galilee and proclaimed the gospel of God.

groups.note: The passive infinitive παραδοθῆναι ("to be handed over") is rendered arrest.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle κηρύσσων is rendered as the finite verb proclaimed.

1:15.sourceText: καὶ λέγων ὅτι Πεπλήρωται ὁ καιρὸς καὶ ἤγγικεν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ· μετανοεῖτε καὶ πιστεύετε ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ.
1:15.targetText: “The time is fulfilled,” He said, “and the kingdom of God is near. Repent and believe in the gospel!”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the καί that joins λέγων to the preaching of 1:14 untranslated.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:16.sourceText: Καὶ παράγων παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶδεν Σίμωνα καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν Σίμωνος ἀμφιβάλλοντας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· ἦσαν γὰρ ἁλεεῖς.
1:16.targetText: As Jesus was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and his brother Andrew. They were casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

groups.note: The participle παράγων supplies the As-clause.
BSB renders Σίμωνος ("of Simon") as his.

unmappedSource.reason: English begins the temporal clause without the narrative connective καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle παράγων.
The English finite clause resumes the two brothers; the participle ἀμφιβάλλοντας has no pronoun.

1:17.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου, καὶ ποιήσω ὑμᾶς γενέσθαι ἁλεεῖς ἀνθρώπων.
1:17.targetText: “Come, follow Me,” Jesus said, “and I will make you fishers of men.”

groups.note: Δεῦτε ὀπίσω μου ("come after me") is rendered Come, follow Me.
ποιήσω with the infinitive γενέσθαι ("make you become") is rendered I will make.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after said.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:18.sourceText: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀφέντες τὰ δίκτυα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.
1:18.targetText: And at once they left their nets and followed Him.

unmappedTarget.reason: English coordinator; the participle ἀφέντες is rendered as the finite verb left.

1:19.sourceText: Καὶ προβὰς ὀλίγον εἶδεν Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάνην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ καταρτίζοντας τὰ δίκτυα,
1:19.targetText: Going on a little farther, He saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat, mending their nets.

groups.note: The article τόν with the genitive τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου means "the (son) of Zebedee".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; in Greek αὐτούς is still the object of εἶδεν (He saw).

1:20.sourceText: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκάλεσεν αὐτούς· καὶ ἀφέντες τὸν πατέρα αὐτῶν Ζεβεδαῖον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ μετὰ τῶν μισθωτῶν ἀπῆλθον ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ.
1:20.targetText: Immediately Jesus called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed Him.

groups.note: ἀπῆλθον ὀπίσω ("went away after") is rendered followed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἐκάλεσεν.
English coordinator; the participle ἀφέντες is rendered as the finite verb left.

1:21.sourceText: Καὶ εἰσπορεύονται εἰς Καφαρναούμ· καὶ εὐθὺς τοῖς σάββασιν εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ἐδίδασκεν.
1:21.targetText: Then Jesus and His companions went to Capernaum, and right away Jesus entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and began to teach.

groups.note: εἰσελθὼν εἰς ("having gone into") is rendered entered.
The imperfect ἐδίδασκεν is rendered began to teach.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the plural verb ending of εἰσπορεύονται.
English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle εἰσελθών.
English coordinator; the participle εἰσελθών is rendered as the finite verb entered.

1:22.sourceText: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ· ἦν γὰρ διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ὡς ἐξουσίαν ἔχων, καὶ οὐχ ὡς οἱ γραμματεῖς.
1:22.targetText: The people were astonished at His teaching, because He taught as one who had authority, and not as the scribes.

groups.note: The periphrastic ἦν διδάσκων ("was teaching") is rendered He taught.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτούς (them) unexpressed after taught.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of ἐξεπλήσσοντο.

1:23.sourceText: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἦν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν ἄνθρωπος ἐν πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ, καὶ ἀνέκραξεν
1:23.targetText: Suddenly a man with an unclean spirit cried out in the synagogue:

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB recasts "there was a man ... and he cried out" as one clause, leaving ἦν (was) and καί unexpressed.
BSB does not render αὐτῶν (their) with synagogue.

1:24.sourceText: λέγων Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ; ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς. οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ Ἅγιος τοῦ Θεοῦ.
1:24.targetText: “What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”

groups.note: The idiom Τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί ("what to us and to you?") is rendered What do You want with us.

studyHeads.note: σοί ("to you") is the one addressed.
ἡμῖν ("to us") is rendered with us.

unmappedSource.reason: The participle λέγων (saying) is represented only by the colon that ends 1:23.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies question support for the idiom; the Greek has no verb.
English verbalizes the idiom with want; the Greek has no verb of wanting.

1:25.sourceText: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἐξ αὐτοῦ.
1:25.targetText: But Jesus rebuked the spirit. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!”

groups.note: BSB renders the pronoun αὐτῷ ("him") as the spirit.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB separates the two commands with He said and leaves καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with λέγων (saying), which N1904 lacks.

1:26.sourceText: καὶ σπαράξαν αὐτὸν τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἀκάθαρτον καὶ φωνῆσαν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἐξῆλθεν ἐξ αὐτοῦ.
1:26.targetText: At this, the unclean spirit threw the man into convulsions and came out with a loud shriek.

groups.note: BSB renders the pronoun αὐτόν ("him") as the man.
The καί joining the two participles is rendered as the and before came out.
The participle φωνῆσαν with its cognate dative φωνῇ ("crying with a cry") is rendered with a … shriek.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ἐξ αὐτοῦ (out of him) after came out.

1:27.sourceText: καὶ ἐθαμβήθησαν ἅπαντες, ὥστε συνζητεῖν αὐτοὺς λέγοντας Τί ἐστιν τοῦτο; διδαχὴ καινή κατ’ ἐξουσίαν· καὶ τοῖς πνεύμασι τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ἐπιτάσσει, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ.
1:27.targetText: All the people were amazed and began to ask one another, “What is this? A new teaching with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!”

groups.note: The masculine plural ἅπαντες ("all") implies people.
ὥστε ("so that") introduces the result and is rendered and.
The infinitive συνζητεῖν ("to discuss") after ὥστε is rendered began to ask.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
N1904 has αὐτούς (they) as the subject of the infinitive; BSB follows a reading with πρὸς ἑαυτούς instead.
The participle λέγοντας (saying) is represented only by the comma before the quotation.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with πρὸς ἑαυτούς (among themselves), which N1904 lacks.

1:28.sourceText: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἀκοὴ αὐτοῦ εὐθὺς πανταχοῦ εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
1:28.targetText: And the news about Jesus spread quickly through the whole region of Galilee.

groups.note: πανταχοῦ εἰς ("everywhere into") is rendered through.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:29.sourceText: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς ἐξελθόντες ἦλθον εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος καὶ Ἀνδρέου μετὰ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωάνου.
1:29.targetText: As soon as Jesus and His companions had left the synagogue, they went with James and John to the home of Simon and Andrew.

groups.note: εὐθύς ("immediately") with the temporal participle ἐξελθόντες is rendered As soon as.
ἐξελθόντες ἐκ ("having gone out of") is rendered had left.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the plural participle ἐξελθόντες.

1:30.sourceText: ἡ δὲ πενθερὰ Σίμωνος κατέκειτο πυρέσσουσα, καὶ εὐθὺς λέγουσιν αὐτῷ περὶ αὐτῆς.
1:30.targetText: Simon’s mother-in-law was sick in bed with a fever, and they promptly told Jesus about her.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτῷ ("to him").

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

1:31.sourceText: καὶ προσελθὼν ἤγειρεν αὐτὴν κρατήσας τῆς χειρός· καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτὴν ὁ πυρετός, καὶ διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.
1:31.targetText: So He went to her, took her by the hand, and helped her up. The fever left her, and she began to serve them.

groups.note: κρατήσας τῆς χειρός ("taking hold of the hand") is rendered took her by the hand.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for went to; the participle προσελθών has none.
English names the person whose hand is taken; κρατήσας τῆς χειρός has no pronoun.
English coordinator; the participles προσελθών and κρατήσας are rendered as finite verbs in a series with helped.

1:32.sourceText: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης, ὅτε ἔδυσεν ὁ ἥλιος, ἔφερον πρὸς αὐτὸν πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας καὶ τοὺς δαιμονιζομένους·
1:32.targetText: That evening, after sunset, people brought to Jesus all who were sick and demon-possessed,

groups.note: The genitive absolute Ὀψίας γενομένης ("when evening had come") is rendered That evening.
ὅτε ("when") is rendered after.
ἔδυσεν ὁ ἥλιος ("the sun set") is rendered by the noun sunset.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").
The article τούς with the participle ἔχοντας forms the relative clause.
The article τούς with the participle δαιμονιζομένους is rendered demon-possessed.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

1:33.sourceText: καὶ ἦν ὅλη ἡ πόλις ἐπισυνηγμένη πρὸς τὴν θύραν.
1:33.targetText: and the whole town gathered at the door.

groups.note: The periphrastic ἦν ἐπισυνηγμένη ("was gathered") is rendered gathered.

1:34.sourceText: καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας ποικίλαις νόσοις, καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλεν, καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν λαλεῖν τὰ δαιμόνια, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν αὐτόν.
1:34.targetText: And He healed many who were ill with various diseases and drove out many demons. But He would not allow the demons to speak, because they knew who He was.

groups.note: BSB renders "they knew Him" as "they knew who He was".

unmappedTarget.reason: English recasts the object αὐτόν (Him) as an indirect question.
English recasts the object αὐτόν (Him) as an indirect question.

1:35.sourceText: Καὶ πρωῒ ἔννυχα λίαν ἀναστὰς ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον, κἀκεῖ προσηύχετο.
1:35.targetText: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, Jesus got up and slipped out to a solitary place to pray.

groups.note: ἔννυχα λίαν ("very much at night") is rendered while it was still dark.
BSB merges ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ("went out and went away") into slipped out.
The imperfect προσηύχετο ("He was praying") is rendered as the purpose phrase to pray.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.
BSB recasts κἀκεῖ προσηύχετο ("and there He prayed") as a purpose phrase, leaving κἀκεῖ (and there) unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle ἀναστάς.
English coordinator; the participle ἀναστάς is rendered as the finite verb got up.

1:36.sourceText: καὶ κατεδίωξεν αὐτὸν Σίμων καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ,
1:36.targetText: Simon and his companions went to look for Him,

groups.note: οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ("those with him") is rendered his companions.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

1:37.sourceText: καὶ εὗρον αὐτὸν καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ ὅτι Πάντες ζητοῦσίν σε.
1:37.targetText: and when they found Him, they said, “Everyone is looking for You!”

groups.note: BSB turns "they found Him and say" into "when they found Him, they said".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render αὐτῷ (to Him) after said.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the quotation marks.

1:38.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἄγωμεν ἀλλαχοῦ εἰς τὰς ἐχομένας κωμοπόλεις, ἵνα καὶ ἐκεῖ κηρύξω· εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ἐξῆλθον.
1:38.targetText: But Jesus answered, “Let us go on to the neighboring towns so I can preach there as well, for that is why I have come.”

groups.note: εἰς τοῦτο ("for this") is rendered that is why.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render αὐτοῖς (to them) after answered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending of λέγει.

1:39.sourceText: καὶ ἦλθεν κηρύσσων εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς αὐτῶν εἰς ὅλην τὴν Γαλιλαίαν καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια ἐκβάλλων.
1:39.targetText: So He went throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons.

groups.note: εἰς ὅλην ("into all") is rendered throughout.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:40.sourceText: Καὶ ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτὸν λεπρὸς παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ γονυπετῶν λέγων αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.
1:40.targetText: Then a leper came to Jesus, begging on his knees: “If You are willing, You can make me clean.”

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render the second αὐτόν (him) after begging.
BSB joins the two participles without and ("begging on his knees").
The words λέγων αὐτῷ ὅτι ("saying to him") are represented only by the colon before the quotation.

1:41.sourceText: καὶ σπλαγχνισθεὶς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ ἥψατο καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι.
1:41.targetText: Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man. “I am willing,” He said. “Be clean!”

1:44.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ὅρα μηδενὶ μηδὲν εἴπῃς, ἀλλὰ ὕπαγε σεαυτὸν δεῖξον τῷ ἱερεῖ καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου ἃ προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
1:44.targetText: “See that you don’t tell anyone. But go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.”

groups.note: The double negative μηδενὶ μηδέν ("nothing to no one") is rendered don’t … anyone.
The relative ἅ ("what") is rendered the offering.

1:45.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἐξελθὼν ἤρξατο κηρύσσειν πολλὰ καὶ διαφημίζειν τὸν λόγον, ὥστε μηκέτι αὐτὸν δύνασθαι φανερῶς εἰς πόλιν εἰσελθεῖν, ἀλλ’ ἔξω ἐπ’ ἐρήμοις τόποις ἦν· καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν πάντοθεν.
1:45.targetText: But the man went out and openly began to proclaim and spread the news.  Consequently, Jesus could no longer enter a town in plain view, but He stayed out in solitary places. Yet people came to Him from every quarter.

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he; BSB writes the man.
The adverbial πολλά ("much, freely") is rendered openly.
BSB names Jesus for the pronoun αὐτόν ("him").
εἰσελθεῖν εἰς ("to go into") is rendered enter.
